overall: Atlanta is running hot with the current temp and running max both at 91.4°F as of 13:00 ET, still about 2.5 hours before the predicted peak (~15:30 ET). A Heat Advisory is in effect through 8 PM with heat index values up to 107°F, and warming velocity remains positive at +1.8°F/hr (with a recent 30-min spike of +3.6°F/hr), indicating meaningful additional heating is still ahead. Scattered clouds (~38% fraction) may provide intermittent limiting effect, but conditions overall are supportive of continued rise.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful spread: GFS is a warm outlier at 96.5°F while NBM is the cool anchor at 91.1°F; HRRR (92.1°F) and ECMWF (93.7°F) cluster more tightly and align better with the NWS official forecast of ~93°F. The current observed running max of 91.4°F already nearly meets the NBM ceiling, making NBM look like the low-end scenario, while HRRR and ECMWF appear more credible.
max_temp_prediction: The META model (most reliable, fusing intraday observations and NWP) favors the 94-95°F even bucket at 53.5%, with 92-93°F as the next most likely at 42.9% — meaning the active even-bucket market top (92-93°F at 41.9%) may be slightly underpricing the 94-95°F range. Given the still-positive velocity, ~2.5 hours remaining to peak, and the Heat Advisory context, a final high in the 93–95°F range is most probable, with moderate-to-high confidence; a best-estimate point forecast of ~93.8°F reflects the weighted center of the META distribution while respecting HRRR/ECMWF consensus.
